$comment: The starter catalogue (#190). One manifest read by the endpoint and by the tests, so a starter that ships uncovered is not possible. 'file' is the source in this repository; 'saveAs' is the name it takes in a project, and the two differ where they must: portable/implement.md and workflow/implement.md would otherwise both land on ai/prompts/implement.md and only one could be taken. Tiers are ordered; prompts within a tier are ordered. 'automation' (#212) is the wiring for a pipeline step: trigger, approval, output labels — the pipeline is catalogue content, never code. A wired prompt in a tier with a 'requires' (#229) is recognisable but not installable: adoption wires a repository's own grill.md, and no button ever writes one into a repository whose team did not choose the methodology. The workflow tier's implement.md carries no wiring on purpose — it is the same step as the portable implement, and two entries cannot own one trigger.

tiers.title: Starters
tiers.summary: Prompts that assume a cloned repository and, where the Automation names one, a Story. Nothing else.

prompts.purpose: Say what is missing from a story before anybody writes code.
Explain how the part of the code a story touches actually works.
Implement the story on a branch and open a pull request.
prompts.assumes: Push access, and a command line the agent can open a pull request with.

prompts.purpose: Write the tests a story's change needs, and run them.
prompts.assumes: A test command the agent can discover from the repository.

prompts.purpose: Review the change a story produced and report what is wrong with it.
prompts.assumes: An existing branch or pull request to review.

tiers.title: The spec-first workflow
tiers.summary: The loop this product's own development runs on: an idea is interrogated to readiness, proposed as a spec, implemented against it, then closed out with a retro and one commit.
tiers.requires: OpenSpec, and the documents these prompts read — a definition of ready, a retro log, and the openspec/ directory layout. Take this tier only if you are adopting the workflow; the prompts assume all of it.

prompts.purpose: Interrogate a raw idea until it meets the definition of ready.
prompts.assumes: A definition-of-ready document, and product context to grill against.

prompts.purpose: Turn a ready issue into an OpenSpec proposal on a branch, as a draft pull request.
prompts.assumes: OpenSpec, and the spec-review gate as a lifecycle label.

prompts.purpose: Implement a validated proposal on its own branch and mark the pull request ready.
prompts.assumes: OpenSpec, a tasks.md convention, and a work-in-progress limit to check.

prompts.purpose: Close out an approved change: retro, archive, spec sync, then one squashed commit.
prompts.assumes: OpenSpec's specs and archive directories, and a retro log.

prompts.purpose: Record a finding that arrived after a change had already merged.
Report where every in-flight change actually is.
